Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?
A: I'd rather just give the facts of what happened, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving and what happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Katy, Texas, heading home from the store. It was a clear afternoon. A car came
over into my lane while we were both going slow, probably around fifteen or twenty miles an hour, and we hit nose to
nose.
Q: Did you have time to brake before impact?
A: Yes, I hit the brakes as soon as I saw the other car drifting toward me, but there wasn't enough room to avoid it.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt, and did the airbags deploy?
A: I had my seatbelt on. The airbags did not come out, but my knee srtuck the lower part of the dashboard pretty
hard.
Q: Can you tell me about your knee injury and whether you sought medical care?
A: My right knee swelled up within an hour, and I could braely bend it. I went to an urgent care clinic that evening.
They took X-rays and told me it might be a ligament sprain, and I was referred to an orthopedic doctor for an MRI.
Q: Have you been able to return to work or your normal activities since the accident?
A: Not fully. I'm on light duty at my job, and I can't climb stairs without pain. I'm still doing physical therapy twice a
week.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I'd appreciate updates on the claim as it moves forward.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
